questions.heading: Rounding Down Keeps a Packing Plan Feasible, Rounding to Nearest Does Not
questions.stem: A 0-1 model has only <= rows, each with nonnegative coefficients and right-hand side. Its LP optimum has x1 = 0.6 and x2 = 0.3, and every other variable at 0 or 1. Which rounding is sure to give a feasible plan?

options.text: Rounding to nearest, since it moves each value by at most 0.5
options.says: Moving x1 up to 1 adds to every row x1 is in, and a full row can then overflow.

options.text: Rounding both up, since a larger plan funds more of the value
options.says: More value is no help if a budget row breaks; rounding up raises every row's left side.

options.text: No rounding at all, since rounding any value can break a row
options.says: Lowering a variable with nonnegative coefficients can only lower each row's left side.

options.text: Rounding both down, since a lower value never raises a row's left side
options.says: Right: in packing rows, a point that fits still fits after any variable is lowered.

questions.heading: Diving Fixes One Variable, Re-Solves the LP, and Repeats
questions.stem: A dive's current LP point has x1 = 0.55, x2 = 0.92 and x3 = 0.30, and every other variable at 0 or 1. Under fractional diving, which fixing comes next?

options.text: x1 at 1, since 0.55 sits nearest the middle of the three
options.says: Fractional diving takes the least fractional variable, the decision the LP is most sure of.

options.text: x2 at 1, since 0.92 is the closest to a whole number
options.says: Right: min(0.92, 0.08) = 0.08 is the smallest of the three, and 0.92 rounds to 1.

options.text: x3 at 0, since 0.30 is the lowest value of the three
options.says: The rule compares distance to a whole number: 0.30 is 0.30 from 0, farther than 0.92 is from 1.

options.text: x3 at 1, since raising it keeps the dive's LP bound highest
options.says: The rule does not look at the bound; it rounds the least fractional variable to its nearest value.

questions.heading: RINS Solves a Small MIP Where the Incumbent and the LP Disagree
questions.stem: An incumbent is x = (1, 0, 1, 0) and the LP optimum is x = (1, 0.4, 0, 0). Which variables does RINS leave free for its sub-MIP?

options.text: x2 only, since the LP gives it the one value between 0 and 1
options.says: x3 is 1 in the incumbent and 0 in the LP: they disagree, so it is free too.

options.text: x1 and x3, since the first plan sets both of them to 1
options.says: x1 is 1 in both, so it is fixed; RINS frees the variables where the two disagree.

options.text: x2 and x3, since those are where the two points disagree
options.says: Right: x1 and x4 agree (1 and 0) and are fixed; x2 and x3 differ and are free.

options.text: x1, x2 and x3, since the LP point is not a 0-1 plan
options.says: A variable on which both agree is fixed even if other LP values are fractional.
